MUQATIL:12:34-35/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:34-35/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:34-35/r1.claim: God answered Joseph's prayer by turning away the women's plotting and evil; God hears Joseph's prayer and knows him.

FARRA:v2p43/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p43/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p43/r3.claim: Joseph made no direct request; the conditional plea if You do not avert their plot, I will incline to them carries the meaning of a prayer, so God answered it.

TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r1.claim: Although Yusuf did not state a separate request, his complaint that prison was preferable and conditional plea that God repel their plot implicitly asked God to protect him, so God answered that supplication.

TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r2.claim: The conditional wording works pragmatically like a request: as a person may say, 'If you do not visit me, I will harm you,' implying that the listener should visit.

TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p146#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says God saved Yusuf from committing sin with the women, although some of what he feared from them had already befallen him.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r1.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r1.claim: God answered Joseph and saved him from committing the sin with the women, though part of what he feared had already befallen him.

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r2.speaker: ابن اسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2139/r2.claim: God hears what people say and knows what they conceal.

NAHHAS:v2p327/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p327/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p327/r3.claim: God gently protected Joseph; the women's plot may refer to the group or to women generally.

THALABI:v5p220/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p220/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p220/r2.claim: God answered Joseph’s prayer by averting their plot, for He hears his plea and knows their guile.

QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r10.claim: When Joseph appealed sincerely to God, swift relief came; whoever bears hardship for God is taken into divine care.

QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r11.claim: God hears the words of those who ask and knows their inward states.

QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p76/r12.claim: Joseph was imprisoned despite his innocence to protect the ruler’s wife from exposure; in the end God turned authority to him and made her his wife after her suffering.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p108/r1.claim: God is all-hearing of Joseph's prayer and knows the sin he fears.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:34-36/r1.claim: God answered Joseph and diverted the women's schemes so that he did none of what they demanded; God hears his prayer and knows what sin he fears.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p239#2/r2.claim: God answered Joseph’s prayer and turned away their scheme; He hears the prayer and knows their plotting.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r7.claim: The response is mentioned although no prior explicit prayer appears because the conditional request to avert their guile itself carries a plea for protection.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p440#2/r8.claim: God is the Hearer of those who seek refuge in Him and Knower of their conditions and what benefits them.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r3.claim: Joseph's prayer from 'Lord, prison' through 'one of the ignorant' both complains to God about his situation with the women and asks Him to remove the affliction; God's response means granting his wish and preventing the sin by blocking their scheme.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p242/r4.claim: Hearing and knowing are fitting attributes after God answers Joseph's prayer.

TABRISI:12:33-34/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:33-34/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:33-34/r9.claim: God answered Yusuf's prayer and protected him from the women's plot.

TABRISI:12:34-35/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:34-35/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:34-35/r1.claim: God hears the supplicant and knows the sincerity of the prayer and whether an answer will benefit or harm the person.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r3.claim: Joseph's conditional words amounted to a prayer that God turn away the women's scheme; God answered, protected him, and kept him from adultery.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:33-34#2/r4.claim: The scheme may mean the women collectively who pursued Joseph, women generally, or the Aziz's wife alone; the author prefers the general meaning.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r1.claim: God answered the prayer implicit in Joseph's conditional plea and turned away the women's schemes by granting protection, so Joseph accepted the hardship of prison over sinful pleasure.

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:34/r2.claim: God hears the prayers of those who turn to Him and knows their circumstances and what is good for them.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r1.claim: Because Joseph's words included a request and prayer for protection, God answered that prayer and turned the women's plot away.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p187#4/r2.claim: God hears the supplications of those who seek refuge and knows Joseph's condition and the women's condition.

QASHANI:12:34-36/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:12:34-36/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:12:34-36/r1.claim: God answers the heart's secret plea by sacred aid and holy impulse, turning it from the profane to the sacred; He hears intimate prayer and knows the fitting help.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r3.claim: The response to Joseph's prayer has no preceding explicit الدعاء because وإلا تصرف عني already implies a request: Lord, avert their plot.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p273/r4.claim: God's diversion of the plot means he prevented Joseph from sin; God hears those who seek refuge and knows their inner states.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r1.speaker: يوسف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r1.claim: Joseph prefers prison to the indecency they invite him to; recognizing his dependence on God, he asks to be turned from their plot rather than left to his own weakness.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p386/r2.claim: God answered Joseph, turned the women's plot away, and protected him; Joseph chose prison over sin despite youth, beauty, and a powerful, beautiful woman inviting him, seeking God's fear and reward.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r1.claim: God answered Joseph and repelled the women's scheme, fulfilling the prior promise that God would turn evil away from him.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r2.claim: God is the Hearer of spoken words and Knower of hidden intentions, answering when purpose is sincere and resolve is pure.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p36/r3.claim: The quoted poetic maxim says that praise can suffice instead of an explicit request, illustrating how generosity responds to an allusion.

DURR-FULL:v4p532/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p532/r7.speaker: بكر بن عبيد الله
DURR-FULL:v4p532/r7.claim: The Aziz's wife later told Joseph that obedience to God had made slaves kings, while disobedience had made kings slaves.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r10.speaker: الشيخ أبو تراب النخشبي
BURSEVI:v4p163/r10.claim: Turning someone already occupied with God away from God brings immediate divine displeasure; nothing equals protection from sin.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p163/r4.claim: Joseph’s prayer asked God to turn away the women’s plot; the verb may govern the prayer directly or govern the supplicant with li, leaving ‘prayer’ implicit.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p163/r5.claim: God turned away their plot as Joseph asked and made him steadfast in chastity, so he accepted prison and hardship over pleasure entailing sin.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p163/r6.claim: God hears the prayers of the distressed and knows their circumstances and what benefits them.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r7.speaker: الشيخ أبو بكر الدقاق
BURSEVI:v4p163/r7.claim: After resisting desire for milk and a beautiful woman, al-Daqqaq dreamt Joseph praised his escape from that temptation and recited that whoever fears God’s standing receives two gardens.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r8.speaker: منشدون
BURSEVI:v4p163/r8.claim: The cited couplet warns that letting the gaze roam exhausts the heart with sights it cannot attain or patiently forgo.

BURSEVI:v4p163/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p163/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v4p163/r9.claim: A person cannot escape the self by relying on the self; escape is possible only through God.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r1.claim: God answered the plea implied by ‘unless You turn away their plot’; the implied request is even stronger than an explicit request to turn it away.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r2.claim: Calling God Joseph’s Lord and beginning the prayer with that address express tenderness; God deflected the plot by sustaining chastity and keeping him from sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p236/r3.claim: God hears the distressed person’s supplication and knows their state, intentions, and what benefits them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r4.claim: The fa indicates God's immediate answer; istajāba is more emphatic than ajāba.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r5.claim: God diverted the effect of their plot by keeping Joseph steadfast and chaste when he was most vulnerable.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p266/r6.claim: “The Hearer, the Knower” explains the prompt answer: God answers quickly and knows pure inward intentions; hearing here means answering a request.

TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#31/r7.claim: A report says the women privately invited Joseph to visit; distressed by their approaches, he asked God to divert their guile, and God answered.

TABATABAI:12:32-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r3.claim: The group seduction was harder than the earlier private trial: many women openly conspired and threatened him, with circumstances favoring them more strongly than the Aziz's wife alone.

TABATABAI:12:32-33/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:32-33/r5.claim: The ending names God as all-hearing and all-knowing, answering Yusuf's prayer and knowing the women's scheme.

TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r4.claim: God’s response and fresh diversion of their guile indicate a new, ongoing act of divine protection.

TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33-34#2/r6.claim: God hears His servants’ words and knows their conditions; thus He answered Joseph by diverting the women’s guile.

TABATABAI:12:33-34/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33-34/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33-34/r6.claim: God’s response concerns the request embedded in the conditional plea to divert their guile, not a request for prison; the next verse explicitly says He diverted their guile.

TABATABAI:12:33-34/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33-34/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33-34/r7.claim: Some took the response as granting a prayer for imprisonment, but the author rejects this: the later wording says only then did they decide to imprison him.

ASAD-NOTES:12:34#n32/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:34#n32/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:34#n32/r1.claim: The literal wording is that God turned their guile away from Joseph.

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: After Joseph passed the brothers’ jealousy and enmity, a second, tougher test began when the Egyptian official’s wife tried to seduce him; it led to unjust imprisonment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: As in the first trial, God granted Joseph great success in this second phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Joseph prayed after exhausting his own strength in guarding his faith and choosing prison over elite women’s seduction.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: When God’s servant perseveres, entrusts himself to God, and asks for help, his prayer is accepted immediately; Joseph escaped the women’s lustful trap.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God hears His servants’ requests and prayers and knows what is in their hearts.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:34/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:34/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:34/r1.claim: God answered Joseph’s prayer and turned the women’s plot away from him; God hears and knows fully.

STUDYQURAN:12:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:34/r1.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:12:34/r1.claim: God strengthened Joseph’s resistance to the women so that he accepted prison’s hardships.

STUDYQURAN:12:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:34/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:34/r2.claim: The Quran links supplication with God’s response, as in 40:60.
